items.description: Anita Anand and William Dalrymple unpack how Britain's empire shaped the Caribbean - essential context for Papa-T's Guyana

items.description: Clear, exam-focused breakdowns of poetic technique that transfer directly to analysing Papa-T's structure and voice

items.description: John Green explains the ideology behind British imperialism - the 'civilising' culture Papa-T recites and quietly resists

items.title: The Poetry Archive - Poets Reading Their Own Work
items.description: Hear poets read their own poems aloud, the same act of recitation and memory at the heart of D'Aguiar's poem

items.title: Amazing Grace (2006)
items.description: The campaign against the British slave trade - the empire's darker legacy behind the polished verses Papa-T recites

items.title: The Long Walk to Freedom
items.description: A colonised man's journey from admiring to dissenting against empire - a parallel arc to Papa-T's quiet rebellion

items.title: Small Island (2009)
items.description: Andrea Levy's adaptation of Caribbean lives shaped by the British Empire - the same colonial inheritance D'Aguiar writes about

items.title: Black and British: A Forgotten History (2016)
items.description: David Olusoga traces the entangled history of Britain and its empire - vital background for the poem's colonial setting

items.title: Empire (2012)
items.description: Jeremy Paxman's series on how the British Empire was built and remembered - the world Papa-T's grandfather lived inside
